entries.note: Three decisions that are not visible from the code alone. (1) A key in the wrong facet is refused TWICE and deliberately: the schema's additionalProperties:false says the key is unknown, and this rule says which facet owns it. Only the second tells a human what to do, and only the first survives if the facet key sets ever change, so neither is redundant. (2) poweredBy is checked for PRESENCE, not truth, and since charter D45 (spec 112) it is refused on EITHER facet rather than earned on the library one: the key left the manifest because an adoption is recorded by the owner's sign-off in a spec, not claimed by the project that made it. Presence rather than truth still matters for the same reason it did before — poweredBy:false is the removed key too, and reading the value would let a declaration carry it silently. This rule is not redundant with the schema's additionalProperties:false: deleting it leaves the document still refused, but the reader is told only that the key is unknown, never where the record went. That is sabotage S3 in spec 112. (Historical note: while the key existed, inverting its facet condition left every structural check green — sabotage S9 in the evidence document was caught by the ACCEPTANCE test, not by any refusal test.) (3) Nothing here opens a file. library.path and plugin.module are shape-checked and confined but never stat'ed, and pin.revision is never compared against bytes, because identifying bytes is acquisition and KI-008 has not decided it; a pack that has not been fetched is a missing prerequisite, not a malformed declaration. plugin.abi is shape-checked and never parsed, ordered or compared — its meaning belongs to the plugin-ABI lane, not to this reader.

entries.note:
A malformed, oversized or unknown-contract declaration is returned as { declared: true, error, formats: [] } rather than thrown: the listing route shows it and the workspace, editor and other roots keep working. Structural (schema) problems are reported before cross-field rules run, and the cross-field pass guards every shape it touches, because a thrown TypeError here surfaced as a 500 that left native editors waiting (review finding 2). Only the first three problems are reported to keep the status line readable. Later contracts are read in stages: the contract-1 part (everything but dashboard and games) decides error/formats, then the shared section helper validates each optional block on its own into dashboard/dashboardError and games/gamesError. The SECTIONS table gives each block the contract it needs — dashboard 2, games 3, devices 4, tracker 5, languageServers 7, packs 9 — so a block under too low a contract is reported by name and ignored instead of disabling previews, and the two blocks stay independent of each other. Spec 085 accepts a root record carrying declarationFile, while string callers retain project-local discovery. The selected filename is returned as source and used in every error. An explicitly missing external declaration is an error, never absence and never permission to read the project-local file. Pass the complete root record from every runtime consumer; passing only root.path silently drops the binding. The packs block (contract 9) references nothing and is referenced by nothing, so it settles first in the chain and cannot disturb the devices-then-games-then-dashboard order the others depend on. The contract ceiling is CONTRACTS, and raising it is what makes a new block answer "unknown contract" to an older reader rather than "unknown key". Contract 10 adds `tests` (spec 117), which like packs references nothing and is referenced by nothing, so it settles first for the same reason. It names a file and validates only the path; the manifest itself is the project's artifact and is read where the rows are built, not here — the same split the local inventory already uses.

Ported from `orchestrator/server/formats.mjs` with F156b (spec 129); `readDeclaration` there is a thin client of this. CONTRACTS is the schema's enum, pinned to this module's copy by a test.
